title: Jett and the Gravity Chase
markdown:
Jett the market squirrel was a marvel at counting acorns and spotting the ripest space-berries, his little nose twitching with concentration. Anything a whisker beyond his comfort zone made his bushy tail do a frantic shimmy: belly-flippingly nervous. Good thing he had Orbi, his ever-whirring sidekick.

Orbi was a hoverbot, sleek and round like a polished moon rock, one big blue eye glowing all-systems-go. Best pal. Well-calibrated balance. He could whiz, whirr, and calculate faster than you could say zero-gravity sneeze: a silent ballet of efficiency.

Their home was a bustling colony on the edge of the Whispering Nebula, where gravity could be a bit unpredictable. Most days it was just extra spring in a leap. This market day was buzzing like a hive of glow-bugs. Stalls overflowed with nebula-gems that twinkled like captured starlight, and singing space-cucumbers humming cheerful tunes. Jett was meticulously sorting sun-dusted figs when a shadow fell over his stall, smelling faintly of stale asteroid dust and ill intent. Whiskers prickled. That was Silas.

“Well, well, what have we here?” The voice rasped like a bag of rusty marbles down a drainpipe. Stickyfingers Silas: notorious package pilferer, grin that could curdle moon-milk, gap-toothed trouble.

Before Jett could squeak, Silas snatched a package from the next stall: a small velvet box shimmering with inner light, like a captured firefly. Clearly a special gift. Silas’s grin widened. He bolted, cackle like a drainpipe of rusty marbles.

“Hey! Stop! That’s not yours!” Jett’s tail jigged with panic.

Orbi’s sensor flashed red. “Unauthorized acquisition detected. Pursuing suspect.” Hover-engines hummed. He rose from his charging station.

Jett hesitated. He hated running, especially when his stomach did loop-the-loops. But watching Silas clutch that shimmering package sparked a fat that’s-just-not-fair feeling.

“Orbi, wait for me!” He scrambled, little legs a blur of brown fur, and launched from his stall, a surprisingly good jump for a squirrel whose usual adventures involved the highest nut.

Silas did not head for the usual colony exits with their friendly blinking safety lights. He veered toward a rusted forgotten grate, a dark maw leading to old transit tubes that honeycombed the colony’s underbelly: forgotten veins, dark and silent.

“The old tubes,” Orbi exclaimed, sensor pulsing. “They haven’t been used in cycles. Gravity there is significantly lower.”

Jett leaped after Silas and felt it immediately. The first jump was wrong: too high, too floaty, as if a giant hand were lifting him. The second landing was like settling onto a marshmallow cloud. Exhilarating. For a squirrel who got wobbly knees on a high shelf, utterly terrifying. Perpetually about to fall, never quite reaching the ground. Tail in overdrive.

“Whoa! I’m floating!” Panic and a strange nascent excitement, the world’s weirdest trampoline.

Orbi zipped past, sensors scanning. “The reduced gravitic pull allows for extended airborne durations. Silas is navigating the primary tube, sector Gamma-7. Velocity considerable.”

Silas was a blur ahead, hunched yet agile in low gravity. He’d done this before. Bounding leaps, suspended for ages, landing with a soft thud, barely disturbing dust. Dancing on air.

Jett’s heart pounded. He hated falling. He’d once fallen off a very small mushroom and spent an hour trembling. Watching Silas, a thought as surprising as a meteor in a teacup: what if this wasn’t just terrifying? What if it was an advantage? What if Silas’s long floating jumps could be his undoing?

“Orbi! He’s using the long jumps. But in low gravity even a small fall feels like a big one, right? So if he misjudges, or if I can make him think he’s about to fall…”

Orbi’s sensor glowed thoughtful purple. “Affirmative. An unexpected trajectory change, amplified by reduced gravity, could disorient him. The physics are straightforward. The sensory input would be overwhelming for an unprepared subject.”

Jett took a deep breath, ignoring the flutter in his tummy. He remembered an old explorer’s manual his uncle had given him, tattered, smudged: In lower gravity, momentum is your friend and your foe. A slight push can send you further than you expect. A misstep is a long way down. Precision is key.

They reached a junction where disused pathways converged. Silas saw an escape and took a daring leap across a wide gap toward a maintenance platform twenty feet away: magnificent, arcing, pure Silas.

Jett did not try to match it. He remembered his market stall, pushing a heavy crate of space-melons, the feel of leverage. Precision is key. A quick precise push with his hind legs against the wall, angled just so. Then, instead of soaring, he controlled his descent with a twist of body, a little adjustment of tail. He landed just as Silas began to descend, on the same side of the gap, a few feet from Silas’s intended spot.

Silas, expecting Jett much further behind—or a foolishly long jump—stumbled. Ankle twisted on uneven tube floor. He yelped, tumbled. Not a massive fall, but in low gravity the momentum exaggerated. He rolled, a flailing bundle of thief and stolen goods.

“Gotcha!” Jett did not feel like he was falling anymore. He felt in control. The ground felt solid, even dusty.

Before Silas could recover, Orbi zipped in, manipulator arms extending. Precise clicks and whirs. Metallic grip gentle but unyielding. The shimmering package had tumbled free and lay sparkling on the dusty floor, safe.

“Package secured. Suspect apprehended. Excellent work, Jett. Your tactical use of gravitic mechanics was inspired.”

They led Silas toward the colony authorities. Jett walked taller than he ever had. He looked back at the dark gaping entrance of the transit tubes. The fear was still a tiny flicker, a reminder of his usual nervousness. It was overshadowed by the warmth of having used the same precision he used on figs.

The package went back to a kindly elder planning a surprise for a grandchild. The elder’s face lit up like a nebula. Jett’s tail might still shimmy when something surprised him. In the weird floaty world of low gravity, he had found his footing anyway.
